about: Results of the AI editorial review for articles published with the automated label. Not a person's review.

Edits: 2024 onside described as 'fourth quarter onward' (per the NFL.com vote report), the 'every season' touchback sentence limited to balls downed in the end zone (the 2024 report spotted bounce-out-the-back touchbacks at the 30), takeaway on landing spots made precise. DATA RIGHTS: the article reported personnel shares and a defence cross-tab that the writer counted from the 2017 Big Data Bowl plays.csv (nfl-football-ops/Big-Data-Bowl on GitHub). Terms checked 2026-10-02: the repository has no licence (GitHub API license: null); its README says the contest closed January 25, 2019 and points to 'official rules' at ops.nfl.com/big-data-bowl, which now returns 404 (redirects to operations.nfl.com/page-not-found); the repo FAQ only says contest participants are 'invited to share ideas and findings', subject to those rules; the current operations.nfl.com Big Data Bowl page carries no data terms for the 2017 set. Nothing clearly permits publishing derived figures on a commercial site, so every figure derived from the file was removed (57.7%/19.3%/7.8% etc. usage table, the 11,557-play count, the defensive-backs cross-tab, 95.2%, the FAQ and takeaway figures), the 'NFL's own play data writes it as 1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR' claim (format visible only in the data file, not the cited schema) was reworded as our own notation, and both Big Data Bowl sources were dropped. No citable published usage source could be verified, so the concept is now explained without figures: new section on the glossary's 'standard formation' (two backs, one TE, two WRs - quotes 'though some offenses call for two' and 'but some offenses use three or four at a time' verbatim) and a logic table of what each grouping invites; the FAQ 'Which grouping is most common?' became 'What does 21 personnel mean?'. Remaining claims verified: glossary (RB, FB, TE, WR, H-back, nickel back), Formations panel images (11 players; nickel package replaces a LB or DL with an extra DB when the offence uses additional WRs; beginner offence is 21), 2026 rulebook 7-5-1, 8-1-5, 5-3-1. Depth-chart cross-link description corrected to what that article says. App claims (lineup builder; Salary Cap Draft 'exposes the units you skimped on') match dump-catalog football-draft-gm-mode. Links: app, hub once, cornerstone, 3 published related, category. Similarity max 0.020; preflight clean; full dry run clean against a scratch log.

DATA RIGHTS: like personnel-groupings-football, this article reported figures the writer counted from the 2017 Big Data Bowl plays.csv (defensive-back distribution 33.7/51.4/12.6%, base groupings 17.8%/15.3%, 61.2% three-plus-receiver snaps, 11,557 plays, 'almost two to one', 64.8%). The repository has no licence (GitHub API license: null), its 'official rules' link (ops.nfl.com/big-data-bowl) is a 404, and its FAQ only invites contest participants to share findings subject to those rules; the contest closed January 25, 2019. Nothing clearly permits publishing derived figures on a commercial site, so all of them were removed (body section rewritten as 'Base fronts and the nickel package', intro sentence, takeaway, GM point 2, the FAQ 'How often...' replaced by 'Is a base 4-3 or 3-4 on the field for every snap?'), the description no longer promises frequencies, and both Big Data Bowl sources were dropped. Remaining claims verified against the NFL Football Operations Formations panel images (4-3: 'the pass rush is primarily generated by the down linemen'; 3-4: 'comes primarily from the linebackers as the defensive linemen occupy multiple offensive linemen' - both verbatim; 3-4 diagram with the outside linebackers wider than the ends; nickel package panel) and the glossary (defensive end, defensive tackle 'in a 4-3', linebacker three to five yards off, mike/sam/will roles, two cornerbacks and safeties, nickel back 'usually at the expense of a linebacker'). Strategy content is written as explanation, with no claims about specific teams. App claims (lineup builder; Salary Cap Draft wording; QB reads the defence in the career sim) match dump-catalog for both football apps.
